title: Massachusetts naloxone prescribing and dispensing
rule_summary: Massachusetts naloxone access includes patient-specific and statewide standing-order prescription pathways, including dispensing to a person at risk or another person positioned to assist. OTC naloxone and prescription naloxone are separate products: DCP controlled-substance regulations apply to prescription naloxone but do not apply to FDA-labeled OTC naloxone merely because the active ingredient is naloxone.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can apply opioid antagonist requirements to a pharmacy-practice scenario without substituting a nearby rule.
exceptions: FDA-labeled OTC naloxone is a separate nonprescription product and is not subject to DCP controlled-substance regulation merely because it contains naloxone.
Prescription naloxone remains available through patient-specific prescriptions and authorized standing-order pathways.
common_confusions: Treating OTC naloxone and prescription naloxone as one legal product category.
verification_notes: Current Massachusetts DCP advisory and statutory/Board sources checked on 2026-08-14; record now distinguishes OTC from prescription naloxone.
